validation: Reviewed the final proposal at planning head 3b47db8b1a75dbe02d13573b7e311d1e5adb122e against frozen code baseline 2bba4bb4b54c5a8be4ddbe89daf6c1c78df050ed.
The planning range contains only Lemmings contract, phase and immutable prior-review evidence; git diff --check passes.
Server Hello nonce zero, unequal minimum and maximum ticks, and exact zero tick now fault as Protocol/ProtocolViolation.
A valid exact non-zero server tick outside the client range is retained while the client remains AwaitHelloAck and accepts only a coherent TickRateUnsupported rejection.
The accepted handshake remains exactly Client Hello sequence 1 epoch 0, Server Hello sequence 1 epoch 0, Server HelloAck sequence 2 accepted epoch, and Client final Ack sequence 2 accepted epoch.
There is no server-final Ack and the server cannot send HelloAck in the same Step that successfully sends Server Hello.
Client and server Hello payloads advertise their own receive limits; accepted HelloAck size is checked against both client payload limits.
Configured wire and decoded payload limits are enforced from PacketHeader before PacketFraming decoding or attacker-sized decoded-buffer rental.
Canonical LimitsRejected is accepted when no higher-priority observable schema or tick cause exists because rejected HelloAck intentionally omits the private server map.
Schema binding is phase-specific and permits explicit SchemaMismatch delivery while requiring accepted and final-Ack schema agreement.
All Hello, HelloAck and final-Ack semantic mutations have deterministic terminal mappings, lease disposal and no invalid state advancement.
Result remains null during an in-progress accepted handshake and is published only at endpoint-specific establishment.
Client-local canonical topology failure publishes ChunkMapRejected with Topology and no wire reason; non-canonical map failure publishes ChunkMapRejected with ProtocolViolation.
Authority and client scopes are revalidated before acceptance, retries, final acknowledgement and established receive processing.

The rejecting server remains Closing after successful rejection enqueue; client disposal produces RemoteClosed, after which the server publishes the stored rejection and closes without draining MemoryTransport.
Requested initiation, echo, simultaneous close, repeated Close, shutdown direction and all transport terminal mappings are coherent.
Closed and Faulted states release replication collaborators without automatically disposing the owned transport; only Session.Dispose disposes it.
Connected false sends retain semantic intent and uncommitted sequence and rebuild byte-identical packets on the next higher Step.
Transport exceptions propagate unchanged after visible lease and stage cleanup; step index, sequence commitment, retry intent and already committed inbound state are precisely defined.
StepResult Received, Sent and StateChanged meanings, first-step zero, monotonic index rejection and sequence-exhaustion ordering are frozen.
Session Core does not Capture, Apply, build or dispatch gameplay data.
SessionRole, SessionState, SessionError, StepResult, SessionConfig and Session<TWorld> are short, coherent public names with no Unity Main alias.
Zero chunk and cluster identifiers remain valid when registered and topology-consistent.
The security boundary correctly states that framing hashes, nonces and epoch do not authenticate or prevent replay and requires an authenticated external transport.
Owned additions are limited to SessionTypes, SessionProtocol, Session, SessionTests and paired metadata, with README as the only existing file allowed to change.
No protocol, payload codec, framing, staging, replication, existing-test, asmdef, manifest, Unity package or worker-owned Lemmings metadata change is required.
